title: Viniyoga of agniś ca

words.gram: phrase written as one word (M’s spelling of अग्निश्चेत्यनुवाकस्य)
words.role: the viniyoga is ‘of’ this section; it quotes the anuvāka’s first words

words.meaning: gāyatrī, the metre of three lines of eight syllables

words.role: with prāśane: ‘in the sipping of water’
what the mantra is used for

translation.literal: Of the anuvāka “agniś ca”: Sūrya the seer, gāyatrī the metre, Agni the deity, the use in the sipping of water.
translation.readable: Agniś ca mā: seer Sūrya, metre gāyatrī, deity Agni; used for sipping water.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the evening prāśana mantra agniś ca mā manyuś ca (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.31), the mirror of the morning sūryaś ca: there Agni is the seer and Sūrya the deity, here the reverse. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form.
in_the_rite: Evening service, step prasana, before agniś ca (M only).

flags.text: M prints अग्निश्चेत्यनुवाकस्य, dropping the c of agniś ca iti (अग्निश्चेत्यनुवाकस्य); the word is left unsplit in the padaccheda because the printed form cannot be divided into real words. A correction of the text should be considered.
